success_patterns: When the clue's anchor is a landmark, event, institution or border (Temple Square, Chapel Hill, Ciudad Juarez/Chamizal), the agent answered the place the category noun asks for (Salt Lake City, North Carolina, El Paso). It gave the bare name, with no institution word, state suffix or landmark.

Several passages quoted the clue verbatim (J! Archive stub, quiz blog, 'Quiz # Question' snippet) but did not show the answer (Gorky Park, preposterous, polka). The agent used the quote only as confirmation and took the answer from encyclopedia or dictionary passages matching the clue's descriptors, rather than stalling or refusing.

For word-origin and definition clues ('This adjective ... comes from the Latin for "before behind"'), the agent found the dictionary/etymology passages whose gloss matched. It answered with the bare headword ('preposterous'), not the Latin form or a description.

For clues naming sub-varieties ('great horned & screech varieties of these birds') or terse descriptor fragments ('Georgia guy, flag-fashioning pop painter'), the agent answered the umbrella category (Owls) or the one person matching all descriptors (Jasper Johns). It did not pick a sub-variety or leave the fragment unanswered.

patch.reasoning: All 8 successes were clean applications of the existing rules, but three recurring behaviors are not yet spelled out. First, a verbatim clue quote with no answer attached (common on J! Archive stubs and quiz blogs) should be treated as confirmation only, with the answer taken from other passages. Second, place-type slots with a landmark or institution anchor should resolve to the bare containing place. Third, etymology/definition clues want the bare English headword. A short bullet on umbrella-category and descriptor-fragment clues covers the rest. These are compact additions that reinforce what worked and do not overlap with earlier rejected bundles.

edits.target: Do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity.
edits.content: - A passage may quote the clue verbatim (J! Archive page, quiz blog, 'Quiz # Question' stub, 'muffed it') WITHOUT showing the answer. Then the quote only confirms the clue is a trivia item. Take the answer from the encyclopedia, dictionary or news passages that match the clue's descriptors (e.g. 'Moscow park ... murders ... best-seller & film' -> the park the reviews name, 'Gorky Park'). Never answer 'not answerable' because the archive line lacks the answer.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - 'This <state/city/country>' clues often give only a landmark, event, institution or border as the anchor ('lighting of Temple Square', 'university in Chapel Hill', 'boundary with Ciudad Juarez'). Answer the place the passages repeatedly tie to that anchor, as a bare name ('Salt Lake City', 'North Carolina', 'El Paso'). Drop the landmark, the institution word ('University of ...') and any state or country suffix.

edits.target: Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content:
- Word-origin or definition clues ('This adjective ... comes from the Latin for "before behind"', 'This lively dance originated among ...') ask for the English word or term itself. Find the dictionary, etymology or encyclopedia passages whose gloss matches the clue, and answer with the headword alone ('preposterous', 'polka'), not the Latin source phrase or a description.
- When the clue names sub-varieties ('the great horned & screech varieties of these birds'), answer the umbrella category in the plural ('Owls'), not a sub-variety. For a terse descriptor fragment ('Georgia guy, flag-fashioning pop painter'), pick the one entity the passages tie to ALL descriptors (birthplace, medium, signature work) and give its full name as the passages write it ('Jasper Johns').
